major_concerns: Emulator (Mininet) fidelity to production may limit external validity of safety metric.
Construction of 1,200 intent→config mappings risks researcher bias and leakage of sensitive templates.
Validator implementation bugs could conflate model vs verifier failure.
Composite safety-score design is underspecified and may overweight easily-measured components.
Scaling and dataset-release privacy/legal concerns not addressed.
required_design_repairs: Specify exact composite-safety-score formula and justify component weights; preregister primary threshold and score aggregation.
Provide provenance for intent→config creation (sources, synthetic vs consented) and explicit exclusion rules for sensitive templates.
Include independent validator verification: unit tests, ground-truth comparisons, and inter-verifier agreement reporting.
Define emulator limitations and include sensitivity analyses vs emulator fidelity (e.g., alternative topology/parameters).
Freeze and release full prompting, model versions, seeds, trace-schema, and baseline one-shot prompts in preregistration.

major_concerns: Vendor-parsers/verifiers are hard to implement comprehensively; parser gaps may dominate measured failures.
Emulator or execution-check coverage will vary per vendor and may prevent execution-ground-truth for some tasks.
Proprietary/edge syntax features risk being omitted, biasing results toward open/simple cases.
Risk that improvements reflect parser coverage rather than genuine generator robustness.
required_design_repairs: List exact vendor versions, syntactic features targeted, and gap-coverage plan; preregister allowed omission list.
Define protocol for handling tasks with missing emulator execution (e.g., synthetic validator fallback) and report separately.
Include human adjudication for ambiguous parser failures and report inter-annotator agreement.
Predefine matching procedure to equalize task complexity across vendors and preregister complexity metrics.
Release parsers, verifier specs, and test suites used for validation.

major_concerns: Curating a labeled hallucination/policy-violation corpus (~2,000 examples) requires domain experts; synthetic labels may bias results.
Adversaries can adapt to provenance signals; robustness claims need clear threat model.
Provenance collection (retrieval indices) may be sensitive or variable across deployments.
Potential latency/operational costs of provenance instrumentation are not quantified.
required_design_repairs: Specify labeling protocol, annotator qualifications, and inter-annotator agreement thresholds; if synthetic labels used, justify and quantify bias risk.
Define retrieval/provenance pipeline in detail (index, retriever, scoring) and release code/config for reproducibility.
Predefine adversary models and budgets for robustness tests; preregister adversarial perturbation generation procedures.
Include operational-cost analysis (latency/storage) and report detector runtime metrics alongside AUC results.

major_concerns: Results hinge on simulated operator model and assumed LLM failure rates; external validity to human operators is uncertain.
Canary detector model may be optimistic; detection fidelity in simulation may not reflect production.
Policy cost model (operator cost vs incident cost) is underspecified.
No live-human validation planned to calibrate simulated approval behavior.
required_design_repairs: Preregister the simulated operator decision model, its calibration procedure, and validation against any empirical human-behavior studies or proxies.
Specify priors and ranges for LLM base failure rates and justify them from literature or pilot data; include broad sensitivity sweeps.
Define canary detector model and detection-performance assumptions; test robustness to degraded detector sensitivity.
Formalize the cost model used to compute Pareto-optimal policies and provide alternative cost parameterizations in sensitivity analysis.
